title: Liquid Crystal Elastomer-Based Magnetic Composite Films for Reconfigurable Shape-Morphing Soft Miniature Machines
notes: No full text: HYP and DSC nodes rest on the linked text of F3/F4 (the 'previously demonstrated' sentence and the closing sentences of each demonstration), so n1, n24 and n25 are source=text. Two parallel branches meet at the trade-off m2: (1) more MMPs -> more magnetization (n15); (2) more MMPs -> the thermally morphed shape stops following the programmed LCE cone (n20). m2 motivates the 1:2 down-select (n6) that every demonstration uses. Packet defects: the F4a crop holds only the vine schematic row, so the filament/hot-needle video frames that its own caption span describes are in no offered crop (o12 cites figs=[F4], panel_ids=[]); the F2e crop contains panels e, f and g while separate F2f and F2g crops also exist; F1a and F1b crops are cut at the right edge (chemical names truncated, F1a's '1 acrylate' label bleeds into the F1b crop); F3c's OCR cue class is 'micrograph' although the panel is macroscopic video frames with a 5 mm scale bar; F2a's 'Increasingtemperature'/'Decreasing temperature' are legend entries listed as axis labels.

nodes.label: Soft miniature machines need to change their base shape in situ, not just their gait, to work in media as different as air and viscous liquid

requires_unseen: the F3 linked-text sentence that prior multi-modal machines 'always remained as a sheet'

nodes.label: Monolithically embedding hard magnetic microparticles in an aligned LCE should give one film both magnetic actuation and environment-triggered shape reconfiguration
Use a patterned-director LCE of RM257/ST386 with a Disperse Red 1 acrylate co-monomer as the photoresponsive base matrix

attrs.reason: programmable director field plus light responsiveness in one matrix
attrs.image_note: F1a draws the three monomer structures and names them; the names are cut at the crop's right edge but readable in the whole figure
requires_unseen: that the reddish tint and photoresponse come from the Disperse Red 1 component (linked text F1/F4)

nodes.label: Disperse hard NdFeB magnetic microparticles (MMPs) into the LCE matrix as the magnetic constituent

attrs.role: carry a programmed permanent magnetic moment inside the actuating matrix
requires_unseen: particle chemistry NdFeB named only in the caption and the F1b column labels

nodes.label: Sweep the MMP:LCE mass ratio over 0:1, 1:4, 1:2, 1:1 and 2:1, i.e. 0, 3.8, 7.3, 14 and 24 vol% MMPs

requires_unseen: the mass-ratio to volume-ratio conversion (linked text F1)

nodes.label: Program two independent fields into one monolithic film: a patterned mesogen director field and a separate spatial magnetization profile

attrs.image_note: F1a draws the circular director field with its +1 topological defect; F3a draws the resulting sinusoidal local-moment profile in perspective and side view
requires_unseen: that the two fields are set by separate steps (linked text F1 and F3)

nodes.label: Cast and polymerise 25-40 um MMP/mesogen films in rubbed polyimide-coated cells that set the director field

requires_unseen: cell assembly and polymerisation schedule (not in captions; only the 40 um and 25 um thicknesses and the polyimide rubbing are in the linked text)

nodes.label: MMPs sit inside the film thickness at every loading: sparse mid-plane clusters at 1:4 and 1:2, a dense full-thickness network at 1:1 and 2:1

attrs.image_note: film thickness looks comparable across all five SEM cross-sections; MMPs are pseudocoloured magenta, so particle identification depends on the authors' colouring

nodes.label: The patterned circular director field of the LCE survives MMP addition up to 1:2 and can no longer be read once the MMPs block the light path

attrs.image_note: at 2:1 the absence of a four-brush texture cannot separate 'pattern lost' from 'light blocked', so the claim is only supported for the loadings that still transmit

nodes.label: MMPs barely move the nematic-isotropic transition: T_NI stays near 64.5 C on heating and 62.5 C on cooling from 0 to 24 vol%

attrs.image_note: the only movement is the 0 vol% cooling point at 62.1 C, about 0.5 C below the four composite points

nodes.label: Mass magnetization of the composite scales with MMP content, from about 15 emu/g at 1:4 to about 69 emu/g at 2:1
The composite stays hard-magnetic at every loading, so a magnetization profile programmed once is retained without a holding field

attrs.image_note: open loops with coercive field near 7 kOe at all four loadings

nodes.label: A magnetic spring built from the film switches damping profile in situ: the repulsive force at 10 mm drops from 2.7 to 0.85 mN after UV triggering
A monolithic magnetic LCE composite film lets one soft body change its base shape in situ and so switch between locomotion modes and device functions

requires_unseen: the paper's own summary framing (no abstract or conclusions section in the packet)

nodes.label: Keep the MMP loading at or below about 7 vol% (1:2 mass ratio): enough magnetization to actuate while the LCE still dictates the morphed shape

nodes.label: A dense through-thickness MMP network mechanically constrains the mesogen contraction, so the programmed director field can no longer set the morphed shape
Each programmed local moment feels a torque in the external field, and the torque distribution bends the flat sheet into the designed semicircular walker

pairs.cause: Embedding MMPs into LCE film and photopolymerization
pairs.effect: LCE director field maintained in areas without MMPs; elastic repulsion concentrated MMPs near the middle of the film thickness
pairs.note: n8 (cast and polymerise in rubbed polyimide cells) produces both n13 (the patterned circular director field survives MMP addition) and n12 (where the MMPs sit), evidenced by o1 (POM four-brush texture) and o2 (SEM cross-sections). Two qualifications the graph adds: (i) 'near the middle of the film thickness' holds only at 1:4 and 1:2; n12 and o2 read a dense wall-to-wall network at 1:1 and 2:1, so the unqualified MatMech effect is true only of the low-loading half; (ii) the elastic-repulsion explanation for mid-film localisation is not in the graph at all, because no panel in the packet bears on it and the packet text never states it

pairs.cause: Maintained LCE director field with MMPs concentrated near the middle of the film thickness
pairs.effect: Shape-morphing capability (thermal/light-responsive) and magnetic responsiveness retained despite MMP integration
pairs.note: both arms are carried: magnetic responsiveness by n12 -> n15 (15 to 69 emu/g, from o6) and n16 (open loops, coercive field ~7 kOe, from o7); retained shape-morphing by n14 (T_NI flat over 0-24 vol%, from o4) and n19 (helical turns vs temperature, from o5), and the light-responsive half by n11 -> n23 with m5. The graph is stricter than the record on 'retained': n20 (from o3) says that above 1:2 the heated film stops following the programmed cone, and m2 makes that the counter-arm of an explicit trade-off that fixes the 1:2 window (n6, n25). MatMech states the same reservation only as a parenthetical ('deviation from ideal LCE response increased with higher MMP content')

pairs.effect: Multi-modal locomotion and environmental adaptability in miniature soft machines
pairs.note: n19 -> n21 causes is exactly this pair: the temperature-set base shape gives the machine that walks in air, reconfigures in the hot glycerol and swims by helical propulsion, evidenced by o10 and o11 and explained by m3 (torque distribution bends the sheet, with k2) and m4 (anisotropic contraction across the splay field, with k4); n16 supplies the retained magnetization. n22 and n23 carry the other two adaptability demonstrations, and all three support n24. Record defect noted, not fixed in the graph: M3's params quote 'rotating magnetic field (40 mT)' for the locomotion test, but 40 mT is the filament experiment of F4a; the swimmer uses 4 mT at 3 Hz (n21 attrs.condition), and 8 mT and 1-4 mT for shaping and walking
